title: Treasury Sanctions Global Illicit Drug Supply Chain Supporting the Sinaloa Cartel
summary: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's OFAC sanctioned 23 individuals and entities comprising a synthetic opioid procurement network tied to the Sinaloa Cartel, targeting chemical suppliers in India and brokers in Latin America involved in trafficking fentanyl and methamphetamine precursors from Asia to Mexico.
key_points: OFAC designated 23 individuals and entities under E.O. 14059, E.O. 13224, and E.O. 14367 for their roles in the synthetic opioid supply chain
Precursor chemicals including N-Boc-4-Piperidone are sourced primarily from Asia-based chemical companies, with India-based suppliers Sutaria, SR Chemicals, and Agrat Chemicals designated
Guatemala-based broker Barrientos received 116 kilograms of N-Boc-4-Piperidone over a two-month period through J and C Import
One kilogram of N-Boc-4-Piperidone yields approximately 1.83 kilograms of fentanyl, representing roughly 900,000 lethal doses
Sinaloa Cartel brokers Carrillo and Acosta were arrested in Mexico in March 2026; India-based Sutaria and Modi were arrested in March 2025
E.O. 14367 designated fentanyl and its core precursor chemicals as Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMDs)
why_it_matters: This is a law enforcement and national security announcement. It has no direct relevance to financial markets, monetary policy, or macroeconomic catalysts. It does not affect interest rate expectations, Treasury market operations, or economic data interpretation.
important_numbers: 116 kilograms of N-Boc-4-Piperidone over two months
1 kilogram of N-Boc-4-Piperidone yields approximately 1.83 kilograms of fentanyl
Approximately 900,000 lethal doses per kilogram of precursor
